submission.natural_language_explanation: A dense 'running English context' dial: on ordinary lower/mixed-case English prose, and more weakly English-commented code, markup and number lists, almost every token after the first few words sits at 0.2-0.6 of max (so any English sentence of about six or more words is predicted active), while it is ~0 on the text's first token, on sentence-final periods, and on ANY non-English text (French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Russian, CJK...), on ALL-CAPS text, on strings of single letters and on one-to-three-word fragments; preceding non-English words (even one French sentence or a word like 'café') suppress the next several English tokens. It peaks (>0.7 of max) on the second word of a tight English adverb/verb + function-word collocation, mainly a quantifier, determiner or particle right after a frequency/degree adverb or verb ('never once', 'never any', 'always some', 'had no', 'ever come across', 'one of', 'well-known').

rival_explanations: Narrower collocation reading: the unit fires only on the closing function word of a tight collocation (never once, had no, one of, come across) and is inactive on ordinary English prose without such a phrase, so plain sentences like 'I went to the store and bought some milk.' would be predicted inactive.

Broader script reading: the unit fires on any token past the first few positions in any Latin-script text regardless of language, so French, German or Spanish sentences of similar length would be predicted active.

Negative-polarity reading: the unit is a negation/negative-polarity detector peaking on any/no/once/ever after never/not/no, so positive frames such as 'there's always some knowing' would be predicted well below the negated version.

Happy to share this beautiful live show which was performed, recorded and filmed at the Montreux Jazz Festival 2015.
On the 28th of July 2015 Ólafur Arnalds and myself met up at my studio in Berlin, and invited Alexander Schneider and his camera to document it. But instead of ending the session after the first take we continued to improvise throughout the night, ending up with several new pieces written and recorded in 8 hours with no overdubs and no edits.

LA CURA DEI CUCCIOLI L’unità didattica fa parte di una serie dedicata alle specie presenti sull_%_île de Sable, una piccola isola canadese a circa 180 km a sud est della costa della Nuova Scozia nell_%_Oceano Atlantico.
